claim: Members of the ubiquitous SLC11/NRAMP family catalyze the uptake of divalent transition metal ions into cells.
source: Members of the ubiquitous SLC11/NRAMP family catalyze the uptake of divalent transition metal ions into cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the function of SLC11/NRAMP family members.

claim: SLC11/NRAMP family members have evolved to efficiently select trace elements from a large pool of Ca2+ and Mg2+, which are both orders of magnitude more abundant.
source: They have evolved to efficiently select these trace elements from a large pool of Ca2+ and Mg2+, which are both orders of magnitude more abundant, and to concentrate them in the cytoplasm aided by the cotransport of H+ serving as energy source.
evidence: This statement describes the selectivity mechanism of SLC11/NRAMP proteins based on established understanding of their function.

claim: Classical NRAMP proteins concentrate transition metal ions in the cytoplasm aided by the cotransport of H+ serving as energy source.
source: They have evolved to efficiently select these trace elements from a large pool of Ca2+ and Mg2+, which are both orders of magnitude more abundant, and to concentrate them in the cytoplasm aided by the cotransport of H+ serving as energy source.
evidence: This describes the H+-coupled transport mechanism of classical NRAMP proteins.

claim: NRMTs are a distant clade of the SLC11/NRAMP family found in prokaryotes that were proposed to function as transporters of Mg2+.
source: In the present study, we have characterized a member of a distant clade of the family found in prokaryotes, termed NRMTs, that were proposed to function as transporters of Mg2+.
evidence: This statement introduces NRMTs and their proposed function based on prior literature.

claim: The NRMT protein characterized in this study transports Mg2+ and Mn2+ but not Ca2+.
source: The protein transports Mg2+ and Mn2+ but not Ca2+ by a mechanism that is not coupled to H+.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the functional characterization experiments presented in the study.

claim: The NRMT protein transports ions by a mechanism that is not coupled to H+.
source: The protein transports Mg2+ and Mn2+ but not Ca2+ by a mechanism that is not coupled to H+.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the functional characterization experiments, specifically the ACMA assays shown in Figure 4F-H.

claim: Structures of EleNRMT revealed a generally similar protein architecture compared to classical NRAMPs.
source: Structures determined by cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography revealed a generally similar protein architecture compared to classical NRAMPs, with a restructured ion binding site whose increased volume provides suitable interactions with ions that likely have retained much of their hydration shell.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison between EleNRMT and classical NRAMP structures as shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The ion binding site of EleNRMT has increased volume compared to classical NRAMPs.
source: Structures determined by cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography revealed a generally similar protein architecture compared to classical NRAMPs, with a restructured ion binding site whose increased volume provides suitable interactions with ions that likely have retained much of their hydration shell.
evidence: This is demonstrated by structural comparison in Figure 7A-C showing the expanded binding site.

claim: Ions bound to EleNRMT likely retain much of their hydration shell.
source: Structures determined by cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography revealed a generally similar protein architecture compared to classical NRAMPs, with a restructured ion binding site whose increased volume provides suitable interactions with ions that likely have retained much of their hydration shell.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural analysis showing the expanded binding site volume and comparison with other Mg2+ transporters.

claim: Ca2+ is a major constituent of bone and has to be taken up by vertebrates in high amounts.
source: As major constituent of bone, Ca2+ has to be taken up by vertebrates in high amount.
evidence: This is established biological knowledge about calcium's role in vertebrate physiology.

claim: Free Ca2+ is present in the extracellular medium in low millimolar concentrations.
source: Although its largest part is immobilized within the body, free Ca2+ is present in the extracellular medium in low millimolar concentrations.
evidence: This is established knowledge about extracellular calcium concentrations.

claim: Cytoplasmic Ca2+ serves as second messenger and its distribution in the cell requires tight control.
source: In contrast, cytoplasmic Ca2+ serves as second messenger and its distribution in the cell thus requires tight control (Carafoli and Krebs, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Carafoli and Krebs, 2016.

claim: Mg2+ is a ubiquitous ligand of nucleotides and nucleic acids.
source: Mg2+ on the other hand is a ubiquitous ligand of nucleotides and nucleic acids (de Baaij et al., 2015; Maguire and Cowan, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to de Baaij et al., 2015 and Maguire and Cowan, 2002.

claim: The abundance of Mg2+ in the cytoplasm is several orders of magnitude higher compared to Ca2+.
source: Despite the similar extracellular concentration, its abundance in the cytoplasm is several orders of magnitude higher compared to Ca2+.
evidence: This is established knowledge about intracellular ion concentrations.

claim: Alkaline earth metal ions are coordinated by electronegative hard ligands, preferentially oxygens.
source: In their interaction with other molecules, these alkaline earth metal ions are coordinated by electronegative hard ligands, preferentially oxygens, which compensate their positive charges by either full or partial countercharges (Carafoli and Krebs, 2016; Payandeh et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Carafoli and Krebs, 2016 and Payandeh et al., 2013.

claim: Transition metals are distinguished by their incompletely filled d-orbitals.
source: Transition metals are distinguished by their incompletely filled d-orbitals.
evidence: This is basic chemical knowledge about transition metals.

claim: The incompletely filled d-orbitals of transition metals permit coordinative interactions with soft ligands containing free electron pairs.
source: This property permits coordinative interactions with soft ligands containing free electron pairs and allows them to change their oxidation state, which makes them important cofactors in redox reactions.
evidence: This is established chemical knowledge about transition metal coordination chemistry.

claim: Fe2+ plays a central role in oxygen transport.
source: The transition metal ion Fe2+ plays a central role in oxygen transport and, together with Mn2+, it is a cofactor of enzymes catalyzing redox reactions.
evidence: This is established biological knowledge about iron's role in oxygen transport.

claim: Fe2+ and Mn2+ are cofactors of enzymes catalyzing redox reactions.
source: The transition metal ion Fe2+ plays a central role in oxygen transport and, together with Mn2+, it is a cofactor of enzymes catalyzing redox reactions.
evidence: This is established biological knowledge about the roles of these transition metals.

claim: The uptake of transition metals has to proceed with high selectivity to prevent competition with several orders of magnitude more abundant alkaline earth metals.
source: Due to their low abundance in the extracellular environment, the uptake of transition metals has thus to proceed with high selectivity to prevent competition with several orders of magnitude more abundant alkaline earth metals, which would prohibit their efficient accumulation.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the concentration differences between transition metals and alkaline earth metals.

claim: Members of the SLC11/NRAMP family facilitate the transmembrane transport of different transition metal ions by a secondary active process that involves the cotransport of H+ as energy source.
source: They are expressed in all kingdoms of life where they facilitate the transmembrane transport of different transition metal ions by a secondary active process that involves the cotransport of H+ as energy source (Courville et al., 2006; Nevo and Nelson, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Courville et al., 2006 and Nevo and Nelson, 2006.

claim: In animals, SLC11/NRAMP proteins are used for the transport of Fe2+.
source: In animals, these proteins are used for the transport of Fe2+ (Montalbetti et al., 2013), whereas in prokaryotes the primary substrate is Mn2+ (Makui et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Montalbetti et al., 2013.

claim: In prokaryotes, the primary substrate of SLC11/NRAMP proteins is Mn2+.
source: In animals, these proteins are used for the transport of Fe2+ (Montalbetti et al., 2013), whereas in prokaryotes the primary substrate is Mn2+ (Makui et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Makui et al., 2000.

claim: Plant NRAMPs are involved in detoxification processes by transporting noxious metal ions such as Cd2+.
source: Besides the transport of both transition metals, plant NRAMPs are also involved in detoxification processes by transporting noxious metal ions such as Cd2+ (Huang et al., 2020a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Huang et al., 2020a.

claim: The SLC11/NRAMP family is distantly related to other secondary active transporters including the amino-acid transporter LeuT.
source: With respect to its fold, the family is distantly related to other secondary active transporters that include the amino-acid transporter LeuT (Ehrnstorfer et al., 2014; Yamashita et al., 2005), although there is little relationship on a sequence level
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ehrnstorfer et al., 2014 and Yamashita et al., 2005.

claim: Characterized SLC11/NRAMP family members show an exquisite selectivity for transition metals over alkaline earth metal ions.
source: Characterized family members show an exquisite selectivity for transition metals over alkaline earth metal ions, but they poorly discriminate between transition metals (Ehrnstorfer et al., 2014; Gunshin et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ehrnstorfer et al., 2014 and Gunshin et al., 1997.

claim: Characterized SLC11/NRAMP family members poorly discriminate between transition metals.
source: Characterized family members show an exquisite selectivity for transition metals over alkaline earth metal ions, but they poorly discriminate between transition metals (Ehrnstorfer et al., 2014; Gunshin et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ehrnstorfer et al., 2014 and Gunshin et al., 1997.

claim: The ion binding site of classical NRAMPs is located in the center of the protein.
source: This is accomplished by a conserved ion binding site that is located in the center of the protein (Ehrnstorfer et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ehrnstorfer et al., 2014.

claim: A conserved methionine in the binding site of classical NRAMPs serves as soft ligand that permits coordinative interactions with transition metal- but not alkaline earth metal ions.
source: Additionally, the site allows interaction with the free electron pair of the thioether group of a conserved methionine residue, which serves as soft ligand that permits coordinative interactions with transition metal- but not alkaline earth metal ions (Ehrnstorfer et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ehrnstorfer et al., 2014.

claim: The mutation of the conserved methionine to alanine in a bacterial NRAMP homologue converted Ca2+ into a transported substrate.
source: The mutation of this methionine to alanine in one of the bacterial homologues had a comparably small effect on transition metal ion transport but instead converted Ca2+ into a transported substrate, which emphasizes the role of the residue in conferring ion selectivity (Bozzi et al., 2016a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bozzi et al., 2016a.

claim: CabNRMT from Clostridium acetobutylicum permitted growth at limiting Mg2+ concentrations, even in absence of any alternative transport pathways.
source: In the bacterium Clostridium acetobutylicum, the prototypic NRMT (CabNRMT) has permitted growth at limiting Mg2+ concentrations, even in absence of any alternative transport pathways (Shin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shin et al., 2014.

claim: Mg2+ has a small ionic radius and high charge density, making its interaction with surrounding solvent unusually strong.
source: The altered substrate preference is remarkable since, owing to its small ionic radius and the consequent high charge density, the interaction of Mg2+ with its surrounding solvent is unusually strong, which makes the dehydration of the ion energetically costly and therefore requires unique features for its transport (Chaudhari et al., 2020; Maguire and Cowan, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chaudhari et al., 2020 and Maguire and Cowan, 2002.

claim: The dehydration of Mg2+ is energetically costly.
source: The altered substrate preference is remarkable since, owing to its small ionic radius and the consequent high charge density, the interaction of Mg2+ with its surrounding solvent is unusually strong, which makes the dehydration of the ion energetically costly and therefore requires unique features for its transport (Chaudhari et al., 2020; Maguire and Cowan, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chaudhari et al., 2020 and Maguire and Cowan, 2002.

claim: The phylogenetic tree of SLC11 proteins shows a distributed organization with different family members clustering into separated clades.
source: The resulting phylogenetic tree displayed in Figure 1 shows a distributed organization with different family members clustering into separated clades.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: Human DMT1 and NRAMP1 function as H+ coupled Fe2+ transporters.
source: Branches of this phylogenetic tree group proteins from the animal kingdom including human DMT1 and NRAMP1, which both function as H+ coupled Fe2+ transporters (Forbes and Gros, 2003; Gunshin et al., 1997)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Forbes and Gros, 2003 and Gunshin et al., 1997.

claim: The primary function of prokaryotic homologues ScaDMT, EcoDMT and DraNRAMP is H+ coupled Mn2+ transport.
source: prokaryotic homologues including proteins of known structure such as ScaDMT (Ehrnstorfer et al., 2014), EcoDMT (Ehrnstorfer et al., 2017) and DraNRAMP (Bozzi et al., 2019b), whose primary function is H+ coupled Mn2+ transport
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ehrnstorfer et al., 2014, Ehrnstorfer et al., 2017, and Bozzi et al., 2019b.

claim: A small branch of plant SLC11 proteins encompasses putative Al3+ transporters classified as NRATs.
source: Within the plant kingdom, a small but separated branch encompasses putative Al3+ transporters classified as NRATs (Chauhan et al., 2021; Xia et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chauhan et al., 2021 and Xia et al., 2010.

claim: The ion binding site signature is fully conserved in animal Fe2+ transporters, bacterial Mn2+ transporters and most transporters of plant origin.
source: The signature is fully conserved in animal Fe2+ transporters, bacterial Mn2+ transporters and most transporters of plant origin, which all exhibit a strong selectivity against alkaline earth metal ions but poor discrimination between transition metal ions.
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The ion binding site motif is replaced by a DxxN-AxxT motif in NRATs and a DxxG-TxxA/T motif in NRMTs.
source: Conversely, the motif is replaced by a DxxN-AxxT motif in NRATs and a DxxG-TxxA/T motif in NRMTs thus indicating that latter clades would exhibit a different substrate preference (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: EcoDMT efficiently transports Mn2+ with low micromolar affinity.
source: Classical NRAMP proteins efficiently transport divalent transition metal ions with low micromolar affinity, while discriminating against alkaline earth metal ions such as Ca2+ and Mg2+ (Ehrnstorfer et al., 2017; Mackenzie et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations and demonstrated in Figure 2A-B showing Km of 13.5 μM.

claim: EcoDMT shows concentration-dependent quenching of calcein fluorescence due to Mn2+ influx into vesicles.
source: In our experiments, we find a concentration-dependent quenching of the fluorescence due to Mn2+ influx into vesicles containing the trapped fluorophore (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transport assay data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Mn2+ transport by EcoDMT is not inhibited by the addition of Ca2+ or Mg2+ to the outside solution.
source: which is neither inhibited by the addition of Ca2+ nor Mg2+ to the outside solution (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transport assay data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: The EcoDMT mutant M235A is capable of transporting Mn2+ with a threefold increase of its Km.
source: This construct was still capable of transporting Mn2+ with a threefold increase of its Km (Figure 2A, B, E and G)
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transport assay data shown in Figure 2E and G.

claim: Ca2+ became a permeable substrate in the EcoDMT M235A mutant.
source: whereas now also Ca2+ became a permeable substrate as illustrated by the competition of the ion with Mn2+ transport (Figure 2F and G) and the direct detection of Ca2+ transport using the fluorophore Fura2 (Figure 2H, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transport assay data shown in Figure 2F, G, and H.

claim: The EcoDMT M235A mutant does not interact with Mg2+.
source: In contrast to Ca2+, we were not able to detect any interaction with Mg2+ (Figure 2I), indicating that the energetic requirements to transport this smaller divalent cation are higher than for Ca2+.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transport assay data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: The EcoDMT triple mutant M235A/N54G/A232T retained its capability of Mn2+ transport while remaining unable to interact with Mg2+.
source: As for the mutant M235A, this construct folded into a stable protein that retained its capability of Mn2+ transport while remaining unable to interact with Mg2+ (Figure 2J–L).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transport assay data shown in Figure 2J-L.

claim: The mutation of the binding site methionine in EcoDMT is a key determinant for the counterselection of Ca2+.
source: We also confirmed the role of the binding site methionine as an important determinant for the counterselection of Ca2+, which due to its much higher concentration would outcompete Mn2+ transport in a physiological environment.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the functional data showing Ca2+ transport in the M235A mutant (Figure 2F-H).

claim: Structural features beyond the immediate binding site residues are required to transport Mg2+.
source: However, neither the replacement of the methionine nor the conversion of the binding site to residues observed in NRMTs was sufficient to facilitate Mg2+ transport, demonstrating that structural features beyond the immediate binding site residues are required to transport this small divalent cation.
evidence: This is inferred from the failure of EcoDMT mutants to transport Mg2+ (Figure 2D, I, K).

claim: EleNRMT was identified from 82 representative NRMT homologues as having promising biochemical properties.
source: Towards this end, we cloned and investigated the expression properties of 82 representative homologues selected from the pool of 745 sequences of putative NRMTs identified in BLAST searches (Figure 1B). Within this subset, we were able to single out a candidate from the bacterium Eggerthella lenta termed EleNRMT with promising biochemical properties (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on the expression screening experiments described in the methods.

claim: EleNRMT elutes as monodisperse peak from a size exclusion chromatography column after expression and purification in DDM.
source: After expression and purification in the detergent n-dodecyl-beta-D-Maltoside (DDM), we found this protein to elute as monodisperse peak from a size exclusion chromatography column. (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the SEC profile shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Consensus mutagenesis improved the thermal stability of EleNRMT and the efficiency of reconstitution without affecting its functional properties.
source: This approach improved the thermal stability of the monomeric protein and the efficiency of reconstitution without affecting its functional properties (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B-D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the thermal stability data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and functional data in Figure 3D-F.

claim: EleNRMT shows robust concentration-dependent Mn2+ transport activity that saturates with a Km of around 120 µM.
source: we initially investigated transport properties of EleNRMT for this divalent transition metal ion and found robust concentration-dependent activity that saturates with a Km of around 120 µM for either WT or the thermostabilized mutant (Figure 3A, B, D and E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transport assay data shown in Figure 3A, B, D, and E.

claim: Mg2+ inhibits Mn2+ transport by EleNRMT in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: For both constructs, we found Mg2+ to inhibit Mn2+ transport in a concentration-dependent manner, thus indicating that Mg2+ would compete with Mn2+ for its binding site (Figure 3C and F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transport assay data shown in Figure 3C and F.

claim: EleNRMT binds Mn2+ with a Kd of around 100 µM as measured by isothermal titration calorimetry.
source: We subsequently quantified binding of either ion to detergent solubilized protein by isothermal titration calorimetry and found a Kd of around 100 µM for Mn2+, which corresponds well with the measured Km of transport of the same ion
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ITC data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: EleNRMT binds Mg2+ with a Kd of around 400 µM as measured by isothermal titration calorimetry.
source: and a somewhat lower affinity of around 400 µM for Mg2+ (Figure 3G and H, Figure 3—figure supplement 2E, F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ITC data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Transport and binding experiments demonstrate the capability of EleNRMT to interact with Mg2+.
source: Together, transport and binding experiments demonstrate the capability of EleNRMT to interact with Mg2+ thus providing evidence that it might indeed catalyze Mg2+ uptake into bacteria.
evidence: This is based on the combined transport and ITC data shown in Figure 3.

claim: EleNRMT shows concentration-dependent Mg2+ transport as detected by the fluorophore Magnesium Green.
source: By directly assaying Mg2+ with the selective fluorophore Magnesium Green, we observed a concentration-dependent increase of the transport rate (Figure 4C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transport assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: EleNRMT does not show strong evidence for the recognition of Ca2+.
source: However, in contrast to Mg2+, we did in no case find strong evidence for the recognition of this larger alkaline earth metal ion, which has become a transported substrate for EcoDMT mutants lacking a conserved methionine in the binding site (Figure 2F–H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the lack of Ca2+ transport in Figure 4D and E.

claim: Metal ion transport by EleNRMT is not coupled to H+.
source: Whereas such concentration-dependent changes are readily observed for EcoDMT (Figure 4H), there was no acidification of proteoliposomes containing EleNRMT as a consequence of either Mg2+ or Mn2+ uptake (Figure 4F and G), thus suggesting that metal ion transport by EleNRMT is not coupled to H+.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ACMA assay data shown in Figure 4F-H.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of EleNRMTts-Nb1,2 complex was determined at 3.5 Å resolution in absence of additional Mg2+.
source: Datasets collected from respective samples allowed the 3D-reconstruction of a map at 3.5 Å for EleNRMTts-Nb1,2 and at 4.1 Å for EleNRMTtsMg2+-Nb1,2 (Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2, Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Table 1 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of EleNRMTts-Nb1,2 complex in presence of 10 mM Mg2+ was determined at 4.1 Å resolution.
source: Datasets collected from respective samples allowed the 3D-reconstruction of a map at 3.5 Å for EleNRMTts-Nb1,2 and at 4.1 Å for EleNRMTtsMg2+-Nb1,2 (Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2, Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Table 1 and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The X-ray structure of the EleNRMTts-Nb1,2 complex was determined at 4.1 Å resolution from crystals grown in presence of 50 mM Mg2+.
source: This complex structure was subsequently used as search model for molecular replacement for a dataset collected from a crystal of the EleNRMTts-Nb1,2 complex grown in presence of 50 mM Mg2+ and extending to 4.1 Å (Figure 5—figure supplement 5A, Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Table 2 and Figure 5—figure supplement 5A.

claim: Mn2+ was localized in the anomalous difference density at a single strong peak per complex in the equivalent position as the binding site of ScaDMT.
source: This data allowed the unambiguous localization of Mn2+ in the anomalous difference density, which showed a single strong peak per complex located in the equivalent position as previously identified for the binding site of ScaDMT (Ehrnstorfer et al., 2014, Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 5B, C,).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the anomalous difference density shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 5B, C.

claim: Mg2+ and Mn2+ both occupy the same site of EleNRMT.
source: In similar location, we find residual density in our cryo-EM datasets thus suggesting that Mg2+ and Mn2+ would both occupy the same site of the transporter (Figure 5—figure supplement 5D, E).
evidence: This is inferred from the residual density observed in cryo-EM maps shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5D, E.

claim: EleNRMTts shows a protein architecture with 11 membrane-spanning segments organized as two structurally related repeats of five α-helices.
source: It encompasses 11 membrane-spanning segments, with the first 10 segments organized as two structurally related repeats of five α-helices that are inserted in the membrane with opposite orientations (Figure 6A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the structure shown in Figure 6A.

claim: EleNRMT adopts an inward-facing conformation.
source: The protein adopts an inward-facing conformation that is illustrated in the comparison with the equivalent conformations of the transporters ScaDMT and DraNRAMP, which both superimpose with RMSDs of 2.2 and 2.0 Å, respectively (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the structural comparison shown in Figure 6B.

claim: EleNRMT contains a large and continuous water-filled cavity that extends from the cytoplasm to the ion binding site.
source: This structure contains a large and continuous water-filled cavity that extends from the cytoplasm and leads to a pocket located in the center of the protein at the unwound parts of α-helices 1 and 6, which together form the ion binding site (Figures 5C and 6C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the structure shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The binding pocket of EleNRMT is expanded compared to ScaDMT as a consequence of about 1.5 Å shift in the location of backbone atoms and differences in the volume of interacting side chains.
source: Although the bound ion is found at an equivalent position as in the transporter ScaDMT, the binding pocket of EleNRMT is expanded as a consequence of the about 1.5 Å shift in the location of backbone atoms and differences in the volume of interacting side chains (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the structural comparison shown in Figure 7A-C.

claim: In EleNRMT, the replacement of alanine by threonine introduces a hydroxyl group whose oxygen atom serves as additional ligand for ion interactions.
source: whereas the replacement of an alanine (Ala 223) in ScaDMT by a threonine (Thr 224) in EleNRMT introduces a side chain containing a hydroxyl group whose oxygen atom serves as additional ligand for ion interactions (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the structural comparison shown in Figure 7B.

claim: In ScaDMT, the bound ion is tightly surrounded by residues of the binding site and largely excluded from the aqueous environment.
source: In ScaDMT, the bound ion is to a large extent excluded from the aqueous environment and instead tightly surrounded by residues of the binding site
evidence: This is demonstrated by the structural comparison shown in Figure 7C.

claim: In EleNRMT, the replacement of asparagine with glycine and methionine with alanine widens the cavity to leave sufficient space for interacting water molecules.
source: whereas in EleNRMT the replacement of the asparagine side chain on α1 with a glycine and the methionine residue on α6 to alanine in conjunction with differences in the main chain positions widen the cavity to leave sufficient space for interacting water molecules (Figure 7A–C)
evidence: This is demonstrated by the structural comparison shown in Figure 7A-C.

claim: Mg2+ binds to EleNRMT in a partly solvated state retaining much of its first hydration shell.
source: suggesting that Mg2+ binds to the transporter in a partly solvated state retaining much of its first hydration shell.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural analysis showing the expanded binding site volume.

claim: It is a combination of changes in the local environment conferred by side chains and more delocalized changes causing an expansion of the binding site that are responsible for the altered selectivity of EleNRMT.
source: Thus, the EleNRMT structure implies that it is a combination of both, changes in the local environment conferred by the chemical nature of side chains and more delocalized changes causing an expansion of the binding site, which together are responsible for the altered selectivity.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural analysis comparing EleNRMT and ScaDMT.

claim: Proton transport in classical NRAMP transporters is linked to structural features extending from the ion binding site.
source: Proton transport in classical NRAMP transporters was proposed to be linked to structural features extending from the ion binding site (Bozzi et al., 2019a; Bozzi et al., 2020; Bozzi et al., 2019b; Ehrnstorfer et al., 2017; Mackenzie et al., 2006; Pujol-Giménez et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: In EleNRMT, apart from the binding site aspartate and glutamate on α-helix 3, all other positions involved in proton transport in NRAMPs are altered to residues that cannot accept protons.
source: Apart from the binding site aspartate (Asp 55) and glutamate on α-helix 3 (Glu 133) close to the metal ion binding site, all other positions in EleNRMT are altered to residues that cannot accept protons.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the structural comparison shown in Figure 7D and E.

claim: The two histidines on α-helix 6b in classical NRAMPs are substituted by tryptophan and asparagine in EleNRMT.
source: The two histidines on α-helix 6b are substituted by a tryptophane and an asparagine, respectively
evidence: This is demonstrated by the structural comparison shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The mutation of Asp55 in EleNRMT strongly compromises transport.
source: Consistent with experiments on other family members, the mutation of the aspartate in the binding site (Asp55), which is a universally conserved position in all SLC11 proteins, strongly compromises transport (Figure 8A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transport assay data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The mutation of Gln379 in EleNRMT exerts a strong effect on transport.
source: Similarly, the mutation of Gln 379 on α10, a conserved position that was proposed to be involved in ion coordination in the occluded state of DraNRAMP (Bozzi et al., 2019b), exerts a similarly strong effect (Figure 8A and C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transport assay data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The mutation of Thr224 to alanine in EleNRMT has a smaller but detectable impact on Mn2+ transport, reflected in at least a two-fold increase of its Km.
source: In contrast, the mutation of Thr 224 to alanine, the amino acid found in the equivalent position of NRAMP transporters, has smaller but still detectable impact on Mn2+ transport, which is reflected in an at least two-fold increase of its Km (Figure 8A, D and E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transport assay data shown in Figure 8D and E.

claim: The T224A mutation in EleNRMT has a much more pronounced effect on Mg2+ interactions than on Mn2+ transport.
source: In contrast to Mn2+, this change has a much more pronounced effect on Mg2+ interactions, which is manifested in the absence of appreciable inhibition of Mn2+ transport in presence of increasing Mg2+ concentrations and the non-detectable Mg2+ transport when directly assaying this alkaline earth metal ion (Figure 8F and G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transport assay data shown in Figure 8F and G.

claim: The EleNRMT double mutant T224A/G58N shows detectable Ca2+ transport activity.
source: In contrast to the compromised Mn2+ transport properties, this double mutant shows detectable Ca2+ transport activity, thus illustrating that the conversion has introduced structural determinants that facilitate Ca2+ interactions and that change the properties of the binding site to more closely resemble NRAMP proteins.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the transport assay data shown in Figure 8I.

claim: The structural and energetic requirements for Mn2+ transport are lower than for alkaline earth metals.
source: This suggests that the structural and energetic requirements for interactions with this transition metal are lower than for alkaline earth metals.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that EcoDMT mutants retained Mn2+ transport but did not gain Mg2+ transport.

claim: Mg2+ and Ca2+ rely on distinct features of the protein which mediate their interaction.
source: In contrast, our studies have shown transport of Mg2+ but not Ca2+ (Figures 3E, F, H ,, 4A–E) thus illustrating that both ions rely on distinct features of the protein which mediate their interaction.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential transport properties observed for Mg2+ and Ca2+.

claim: The larger size of the binding site in EleNRMT is an immediate consequence of the decreased side chain-volume of the surrounding residues concomitant with local differences in the backbone positions.
source: The larger size of the site is an immediate consequence of the decreased side chain-volume of the surrounding residues concomitant with local differences in the backbone positions (Figure 7A and B)
evidence: This is demonstrated by the structural comparison shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: An octahedral Mg2+-water complex model placed in the binding site of EleNRMT suggests that only one of the solvent molecules would be substituted by a direct interaction with the oxygen of the amide backbone group of Thr 224.
source: Although the limited resolution of our structures does not permit assignment of water molecules, an octahedral Mg2+-water complex model placed in the binding site suggests that only one of the solvent molecules would be substituted by a direct interaction with the oxygen of the amide backbone group of Thr 224, whereas other interactions with the conserved binding site would be mediated by coordinating waters (Figure 9B and C).
evidence: This is based on modeling of the Mg2+-water complex in the binding site shown in Figure 9C.

claim: The distinct structural features of EleNRMT suggest that the binding cavity would be sufficiently big for Mg2+ to retain much of its surrounding water during transport.
source: However, in contrast to DraNRAMP, where the bound ion becomes tightly encircled by protein residues, the distinct structural features of EleNRMT and the lower side chain volume of residues of its binding site suggest that this cavity would be sufficiently big for Mg2+ to retain much of its surrounding water during transport (Figure 9D–F)
evidence: This is inferred from the structural comparison and modeling shown in Figure 9D-F.

claim: It is the larger hydrated complex of Mg2+ rather than the naked ion that is relevant for transport by EleNRMT.
source: thus emphasizing that it is the larger hydrated complex of Mg2+ rather than the naked ion that is relevant for transport.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural analysis showing the expanded binding site.

claim: The absent coupling of metal ion transport to H+ in EleNRMT is reflected in the location of ionizable residues that are conserved within the proton-coupled part of the family and that are absent in EleNRMT.
source: A second pronounced feature that distinguishes EleNRMT and likely other NRMTs from classical SLC11 proteins concerns the absent coupling of metal ion transport to an energy source, which in case of NRAMPs is conferred by the cotransport of protons (Ehrnstorfer et al., 2017; Gunshin et al., 1997; Figure 4F–H). This property is reflected in the location of ionizable residues that are conserved within the proton-coupled part of the family and that are absent in EleNRMT (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the structural comparison shown in Figure 7E and F and functional data in Figure 4F-H.

claim: In light of the high extracellular Mg2+ concentration and the inside negative membrane potential, H+ coupling may not be required for efficient Mg2+ uptake in the natural habitat of the bacterium.
source: It thus appears that in light of the high extracellular Mg2+ concentration and the inside negative membrane potential such coupling may not be required for efficient uptake in the natural habitat of the bacterium.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed lack of H+ coupling and physiological considerations.

claim: The promiscuity of transition metal ion transport contrasts the tight requirements for the alkaline earth metal ions such as Ca2+ and Mg2+.
source: Our work also illustrates the promiscuity of transition metal ion transport, which contrasts the tight requirements for the alkaline earth metal ions such as Ca2+ and Mg2+, latter of which is transported in a largely hydrated state.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined functional and structural data showing differential requirements for different ions.

claim: The observation that the previously investigated NRMT homologue did not permit growth upon Mn2+-limitation could be a consequence of the lower affinity to this ion, the competition with abundant Mg2+ and the absence of an energy source.
source: The observation that the previously investigated NRMT homologue did not permit growth upon Mn2+ -limitation (Shin et al., 2014) could be a consequence of the lower affinity to this ion, the competition with abundant Mg2+ and the absence of an energy source, which might be mandatory for efficient accumulation of the scarce substrate.
evidence: This is speculation based on the functional characterization and comparison with previous studies.

claim: It appears unlikely that the human transporter SLC11A1 would permit Mg2+ transport.
source: In this respect, it appears unlikely that the human transporter SLC11A1, which resides in the phagosomes of macrophages and is involved in the immune response against invading microbes, would itself permit Mg2+ transport as suggested in a recent study (Cunrath and Bumann, 2019).
evidence: This is speculation based on the structural requirements identified for Mg2+ transport and comparison with SLC11A1.

claim: EleNRMT and EleNRMTts have a Km of approximately 119-124 μM for Mn2+ transport.
source: we initially investigated transport properties of EleNRMT for this divalent transition metal ion and found robust concentration-dependent activity that saturates with a Km of around 120 µM for either WT or the thermostabilized mutant (Figure 3A, B, D and E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the Michaelis-Menten fits shown in Figure 3B and E.

claim: EcoDMT has a Km of 13.5 μM for Mn2+ transport.
source: Initial velocities were derived from individual traces of experiments displayed in (A), the solid line shows the fit to a Michaelis–Menten equation with an apparent Km of 13.5  μM.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The EcoDMT mutant M235A has a Km of 41 μM for Mn2+ transport.
source: The solid lines are fits to a Michaelis–Menten equation with apparent Km of 41  μM (Mn2+) and 107 uM (Mn2+ in presence of 2 mM Ca2+).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The EcoDMT mutant M235A has a Km of 107 μM for Mn2+ transport in presence of 2 mM Ca2+.
source: The solid lines are fits to a Michaelis–Menten equation with apparent Km of 41  μM (Mn2+) and 107 uM (Mn2+ in presence of 2 mM Ca2+).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The EcoDMT triple mutant M235A/N54G/A232T has a Km of 31 μM for Mn2+ transport.
source: The solid lines are fits to a Michaelis–Menten equation with apparent Km of 31  μM (Mn2+) and 38 µM (Mn2+ in presence of 2 mM Mg2+).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2L.

claim: The EcoDMT triple mutant M235A/N54G/A232T has a Km of 38 μM for Mn2+ transport in presence of 2 mM Mg2+.
source: The solid lines are fits to a Michaelis–Menten equation with apparent Km of 31  μM (Mn2+) and 38 µM (Mn2+ in presence of 2 mM Mg2+).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2L.

claim: EleNRMT and ScaDMT superimpose with RMSDs of 2.2 and 2.0 Å, respectively.
source: The protein adopts an inward-facing conformation that is illustrated in the comparison with the equivalent conformations of the transporters ScaDMT and DraNRAMP, which both superimpose with RMSDs of 2.2 and 2.0 Å, respectively (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the structural comparison.

claim: Three distinct nanobodies (Nb1-3) recognizing EleNRMT were identified by phage display.
source: These experiments allowed us to identify three distinct binders recognizing the protein termed Nb1-3EleNRMT (short Nb1-3) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is described in the results section on nanobody generation.

claim: Nb1 and either Nb2 or Nb3 were able to bind concomitantly to EleNRMT to assemble into a ternary complex.
source: We thus attempted to further increase the size of the complex and found that Nb1 and either one of the two closely related nanobodies Nb2 or Nb3 were able to bind concomitantly to the protein to assemble into a ternary complex (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the SEC profile shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The phylogenetic tree of SLC11 proteins was generated from 1100 eukaryotic and 447 prokaryotic NRAMP proteins and 745 prokaryotic NRMTs.
source: In this way, sequences of 1100 eukaryotic and 447 prokaryotic NRAMP proteins and 745 prokaryotic NRMTs were aligned and subjected to phylogenetic characterization.
evidence: This is described in the methods section on phylogenetic analysis.

claim: The first hydration shell of Mg2+ coordinates the ion in an octahedral geometry.
source: The first hydration shell of Mg2+, which coordinates the ion in an octahedral geometry (Figure 9A), was thus suggested to remain bound to the ion in its initial encounter with the binding site and probably also during transport.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Mg2+ hydration shown schematically in Figure 9A.

claim: In the structures of MgtE and CorA, the first hydration shell of Mg2+ remains bound to the ion.
source: A similar feature was indeed observed in the structures of the unrelated bacterial Mg2+ transport proteins MgtE (Takeda et al., 2014) and CorA (Guskov et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Takeda et al., 2014 and Guskov et al., 2012.

claim: In the membrane-inserted domain of the transporter CorC, protein interactions are established with a fully dehydrated Mg2+ ion.
source: whereas protein interactions in the membrane-inserted domain of the transporter CorC are established with a fully dehydrated ion (Huang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Huang et al., 2021.
